name: Vincent Yen
summary: Texas A&M computer science student building useful software across geospatial tools, AI, and web applications.
about: I'm Vincent, a Texas A&M computer science student minoring in cybersecurity. I like building software that makes complicated work easier to navigate, from weather-aware flight routing to turning a learning goal into a concrete plan.
outsideOfCode: Outside class, I follow sports, film Aggie football, spend time with friends, listen to music, cook, and travel.
education: Texas A&M University · B.S. Computer Science · Cybersecurity minor · Expected May 2028

experience.summary: Delivered 20+ production enhancements to USAA's React 18 Auto Digital First Notice of Loss application, part of a claims platform handling 600K-670K auto claims annually.
highlights: Resolved React Context synchronization across dynamically added vehicles, passengers, drivers, and incident details.
Fixed API payload mismatches between React and Java Spring Boot services that caused invalid claim submissions.
Added conditional Formik and Yup validation across 35+ claim workflow sections.

experience.company: The University of Texas at Dallas
experience.summary: Built a BERT-based text simplification tool and fine-tuned TensorFlow NLP models with a five-person accessibility research team.
highlights: Reached over 85% accuracy on long-text summaries.
Reduced model training time by 25% while improving classification accuracy by 10%.
Helped integrate machine-learning prototypes into deployable accessibility tools.

images.alt: TAMUFlight mission control map showing flights and proposed reroutes.

projects.summary: A real-time flight disruption dashboard for airport operations: track aircraft, monitor live weather, and find alternate routes around storms.
highlights: Visualizes live flights, precipitation radar, cloud cover, and storm events on a Mapbox map.
Uses Dijkstra's algorithm to find weather-aware routes and prioritize emergency flights.
Combines cache-first API access, GPU detection, and client-side route calculations for responsive analysis.

projects.summary: A location-aware grocery search that compares nearby prices, stock, and availability so shoppers can find a better deal within 10 miles.
highlights: Connects Walmart and Kroger product data, handling HMAC signing and OAuth 2.0 authentication.
Normalizes different retailer responses and filters stores by distance with the Haversine formula.
Caches searches in MongoDB to reduce repeated API requests.

projects.summary: An AI learning planner that turns a broad goal into clear steps, then organizes the goal and tasks in the learner's Notion workspace.
highlights: Uses Gemini to turn a learning goal into a structured plan and actionable to-do list.
Creates a dedicated Notion page and task database through the Notion API.
Built with a Python and Flask workflow, including input validation and API error handling.
